questionText: In an in-vitro fertilization (IVF) programme, if the embryo has developed past the 8-cell stage (more than 8 blastomeres), it is transferred into the uterus in a procedure called:

options.text: Intra-Uterine Transfer (IUT)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT)'.

options.text: Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer (GIFT)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer (GIFT)'.

options.text: Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI)'.

detailedSolution:
1. Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus (IUT - intra uterine transfer), to complete their further development.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) is recommended for a female who:

options.text: Cannot produce an ovum, but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further development
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Has completely blocked fallopian tubes bilaterally
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Has completely blocked fallopian tubes bilaterally'.

options.text: Produces defective cervical mucus that coagulates sperms
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Produces defective cervical mucus that coagulates sperms'.

options.text: Cannot implant a blastocyst due to uterine fibroids
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Cannot implant a blastocyst due to uterine fibroids'.

detailedSolution:
1. Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube (GIFT – gamete intra fallopian transfer) of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilization and further development is another method attempted.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is a specialized ART procedure in which:

options.text: A single sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of an ovum in the laboratory
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Semen is artificially introduced into the fallopian tube via catheter
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Semen is artificially introduced into the fallopian tube via catheter'.

options.text: Multiple sperms are incubated with an unfertilized morula
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Multiple sperms are incubated with an unfertilized morula'.

options.text: Sperm nuclei are fused with an enucleated somatic cell
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Sperm nuclei are fused with an enucleated somatic cell'.

detailedSolution:
1. Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is another specialized procedure to form an embryo in the laboratory in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: Intra-Uterine Insemination (IUI) is particularly useful in treating cases of infertility where:

options.text: The male partner is unable to inseminate or has very low sperm counts (oligozoospermia)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: The female partner has blocked fallopian tubes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The female partner has blocked fallopian tubes'.

options.text: The female has absence of ovaries
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The female has absence of ovaries'.

options.text: The fetus suffers from down syndrome
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The fetus suffers from down syndrome'.

detailedSolution:
1. Infertility cases either due to inability of the male partner to inseminate the female or due to very low sperm counts in the ejaculates, could be corrected by artificial insemination (AI) technique.
2. In this technique, the semen collected either from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI – intra-uterine insemination) of the female.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In molecular genetics analysis #171: During DNA replication, if RNA primers are synthesized by primase in the 5' -> 3' direction, why is an RNA primer mandatory for DNA polymerase to commence chain elongation?

options.text: DNA-dependent DNA polymerase cannot initiate DNA synthesis de novo and requires a free 3'-OH group to attach the incoming deoxynucleotide
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: RNA primer unwinds the double helix by breaking hydrogen bonds
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'RNA primer unwinds the double helix by breaking hydrogen bonds'.

options.text: RNA primer stabilizes the single-stranded DNA binding proteins
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'RNA primer stabilizes the single-stranded DNA binding proteins'.

options.text: DNA polymerase can only recognize ribose sugars at the active site
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'DNA polymerase can only recognize ribose sugars at the active site'.

detailedSolution:
1. DNA polymerases cannot initiate synthesis of a DNA strand de novo.
2. They require a pre-existing 3'-OH group (provided by the RNA primer synthesized by primase) to catalyze the formation of the phosphodiester bond.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In evolutionary biology study #69: Coelacanth (lobefin), caught in South Africa in 1938, was thought to be extinct. Why is the Coelacanth of immense evolutionary significance?

options.text: It represents the ancestor of modern amphibians that first crawled on land and evolved into terrestrial tetrapods
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: It is the direct ancestor of modern flying birds
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It is the direct ancestor of modern flying birds'.

options.text: It is the oldest known mammal with placental nourishment
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It is the oldest known mammal with placental nourishment'.

options.text: It provides fossil evidence of angiosperm pollination
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'It provides fossil evidence of angiosperm pollination'.

detailedSolution:
1. In 1938, a fish caught in South Africa happened to be a Coelacanth which was thought to be extinct.
2. These animals called lobefins evolved into the first amphibians that lived on both land and water.
Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In industrial biotechnology evaluation #103: Alcoholic beverages such as wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth. Why is distillation employed for the latter group?

options.text: Distillation increases the alcohol concentration because yeast cells are inhibited when alcohol content exceeds 13-14% during natural fermentation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Distillation eliminates toxic methanol completely
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Distillation eliminates toxic methanol completely'.

options.text: Distillation adds organic fruit flavours
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Distillation adds organic fruit flavours'.

options.text: Distillation introduces bacterial cultures for second fermentation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Distillation introduces bacterial cultures for second fermentation'.

detailedSolution:
1. Wine and beer are produced without distillation whereas whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.
2. Natural fermentation ceases when yeast poisoning occurs at ~13% alcohol; distillation concentrates the ethanol to higher proof.
Hence, Option A is correct.

detailedSolution:

Hence, Option A is correct.

questionText: In molecular diagnostic testing #103: When using a radioactive single-stranded probe to detect a mutated gene in cloned host cells via autoradiography, why does the mutated gene NOT appear on the photographic film?

options.text: The radioactive probe cannot hybridize with the mutated gene because of lack of nucleotide sequence complementarity
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: The mutated gene emits gamma radiation that destroys the photographic emulsion
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The mutated gene emits gamma radiation that destroys the photographic emulsion'.

options.text: The probe binds irreversibly to nitrocellulose membranes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The probe binds irreversibly to nitrocellulose membranes'.

options.text: The mutated gene is digested by host nucleases within the gel
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'The mutated gene is digested by host nucleases within the gel'.

detailedSolution:
1. A single stranded DNA or RNA, tagged with a radioactive molecule (probe) is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells.
2. The clone having the mutated gene will hence not appear on the photographic film, because the probe will not have complementarity with the mutated gene.
Hence, Option A is correct.

topic: Global Biodiversity Patterns and Threats Concept #103
questionText: In biodiversity conservation assessment #103: Tropical Amazonian rainforest in South America harbours the greatest biodiversity on Earth. Why do the tropics support vastly greater biological diversity than temperate regions?

options.text: Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, are less seasonal, more predictable, and receive higher solar energy
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Consistent with NCERT Biology principles.

options.text: Tropical environments experience frequent glaciations promoting rapid speciation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Tropical environments experience frequent glaciations promoting rapid speciation'.

options.text: Tropical soils contain higher calcium carbonate concentrations
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Tropical soils contain higher calcium carbonate concentrations'.

options.text: Predators are completely absent from tropical ecosystems
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses concept details with distractor 'Predators are completely absent from tropical ecosystems'.

detailedSolution:
1. Ecologists propose three major hypotheses for high tropical diversity: (a) Speciation is a function of time; tropics remained undisturbed unlike glaciated temperate regions; (b) Tropical environments are less seasonal, more constant and predictable; (c) More solar energy is available in the tropics, contributing to higher productivity.
Hence, Option A is correct.
